title: Sleeping well in the early modern world: an environmental approach to the history of sleep care
summary: History of how people sought healthy sleep c.1500-1750 in Britain, Ireland and early American colonies: environmental practices, bedding, soporific tonics, and medical, botanical and climatic knowledge about sleep; informs debates on environments and healthy or unhealthy sleep habits.

title: Suicide Cultures: Reimagining Suicide Research
summary: Qualitative mixed-methods study of the social contexts and cultural meanings of suicide in communities across Scotland: reviews of suicide cases, interviews with bereaved people and with people who have self-harmed, arts-based and ethnographic work.

title: Crafting Contention: The role of zines in contesting mental health knowledge and practice
summary: Analysis and co-production of zines made by people with lived experience of mental distress; how they challenge psychiatric understandings and diagnoses; aims to inform learning, reduce stigma and shape mental health policy and practice.

title: The Biosocial Lives of Birth Cohorts
summary: Ethnographic study of birth cohort studies in the UK, Europe and Latin America as infrastructure for biosocial science; aims to inform new methods for birth cohort research.

title: Orphan drugs: high prices, access to medicines and the transformation of biopharmaceutical innovation
summary: Study of orphan drugs for rare diseases, their high prices and refusals to fund them, and 'orphanisation' of biopharmaceutical innovation in the UK and USA; implications for industry, health policy and patient access.

title: Investing in mental health promotion across the life-course
summary: How schools and workplaces decide to invest in mental health promotion: mapping attitudes, resource use, use of evidence and decision-making; guidance for policymakers on mental health promotion.

title: North and South: Regional Health Inequalities in England
summary: Mixed-method, multidisciplinary account of the north-south health divide in England since the 19th century: its causes, change over time and lived experience, in European context; insights into closing health inequalities.

title: Maps of Malignancy: Epidemiologists and Cancer in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Archival and ethnographic study of epidemiological cancer mapping in sub-Saharan Africa over 70 years and how it shaped cancer imaginaries and health policy.

title: Addressing Infertility in Emergent Reproductive Markets: An Anthropology of Cross-Border Reproductive Care in Contemporary Central Asia
summary: Anthropology of how people in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan address involuntary childlessness: fertility care sites, cross-border reproductive care, assisted reproduction ethics, and how policy, law and religion shape these markets.

title: Equity & difference: Deconstructing gender in health research for women
summary: Empirical ethics study of persistent structural barriers to women's health in how research is designed, conducted and translated, and how arguments to prioritise women's and girls' health needs are received.

title: 'The Last Taboo of Motherhood?': Postnatal Mental Disorders in Twentieth-Century Britain
summary: History of postnatal mental illness in 20th-century Britain: psychiatric classification and practice, mental hospital admissions, infanticide defence pleas, services and treatments, and social attitudes to motherhood.
